Parturition:

Parturition is the process of childbirth or delivery of the fetus.

It begins with strong uterine contractions at the end of pregnancy.

Parturition is triggered by a neuroendocrine mechanism involving signals from the fully
developed fetus and placenta.

These signals cause mild contractions known as the fetal ejection reflex.


The reflex triggers the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary gland.

Oxytocin causes stronger uterine contractions, which stimulate more oxytocin release.

This positive feedback loop results in increasingly strong contractions, leading to the
expulsion of the baby through the birth canal.

After delivery, the placenta is also expelled from the uterus.
